raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Kimi K3's hybrid attention backend processes mixed prefill/decode batches through the existing extend path. Decode histories may end in partially filled KV pages. Gathering whole pages leaves invalid prefix-tail positions between requests, while prefix FIA uses cumulative logical sequence lengths. This mismatch can cause attention length errors or incorrect request boundaries. ## Modifications - Build valid prefix-token indices and cumulative prefix lengths once per batch. - Reuse ND/NZ page gathering, then compact latent KV and RoPE before kv_b_proj. - Update both MLA prefix branches to consume the compacted tensors. - Preserve the [tokens, 1, head_dim] RoPE shape by removing redundant flattening. - Reuse the existing extend, FIA, and LSE-merge pipeline. - Add four regression tests covering partial, empty, and aligned prefixes, shared/reordered pages, ND/NZ layouts, and real cache dimensions. ## Accuracy Tests - Four CPU/NPU cache-layout regression tests passed. - Four native FIA reference cases passed against independent FP32 full attention, including partial pages and zero-length prefixes. Maximum absolute error: 0.003689, with atol=0.006 and rtol=0.03. - Reduced four-layer Kimi K3 serving validation passed with TP4 and graphs disabled: 3/3 requests completed, with 14 actual mixed batches per worker. Model-level accuracy remains unresolved: reduced-model logits comparisons did not pass the screening thresholds, and off/off repeats also showed differences. These results do not establish model-level accuracy parity. Full 93-layer model quality has not been validated. ## Speed Tests and Profiling A request with 2,048 input tokens and 2,048 output tokens was started first. After its 64th output token, a second request with 131,072 input tokens and one output token was submitted. The comparison used the same revision with mixed chunk disabled/enabled, a chunk budget of 1,024, page size 128, and non-speculative decoding. Decode graphs were enabled and prefill graphs disabled. Four measured runs were collected per setting, excluding warmups. | Metric | Mixed chunk disabled | Mixed chunk enabled | |---|---:|---:| | Maximum observed short-request ITL across all four runs | 9.120 s | 188.7 ms | | Short requests experiencing a token gap exceeding 1 s | 4/4 | 0/4 | | Mean short-request TPOT | 9.140 ms | 9.231 ms | | Mean short-request E2E | 18.894 s | 19.099 s | | Mean long-request TTFT | 8.995 s | 9.861 s | Each enabled run recorded 129 genuine mixed batches, with each batch advancing the short request by one decode token alongside the long request's prefill. The maximum observed token gap decreased by approximately 98%, and no second-scale gaps occurred in the four enabled samples. This demonstrates reduced prefill-induced decode starvation and improved streaming continuity in this scenario. Mean TPOT and E2E showed no stable improvement. These results compare the scheduling configurations on the same revision; they do not isolate the prefix-packing overhead or establish full-model, P99-latency, or throughput improvements. No operator profiling was collected for this test. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #41642488933](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41642488933) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41642488684](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41642488684) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #41642488750](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41642488750) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. -"""Read logical pages from the explicit PA-NZ storage of the NPU MLA cache."""
+"""Read pages or compact logical tokens from the NPU MLA cache."""
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
 
 import torch
 
 
+def build_mla_prefix_token_indices(
+    prefix_lens: Sequence[int], page_size: int, *, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Select valid tokens from request-major, whole-page prefix gathers.
+
+    Each request owns ceil(prefix_len / page_size) gathered pages. Its valid
+    tokens start at that physical page offset, not at sum(previous lengths).
+    Build this once per batch and reuse it for latent and RoPE at every layer.
+    """
+    indices = []
+    page_offset = 0
+    for prefix_len in prefix_lens:
+        if prefix_len:
+            indices.append(
+                torch.arange(page_offset, page_offset + prefix_len, dtype=torch.int64)
+            )
+        page_offset += (prefix_len + page_size - 1) // page_size * page_size
+    if not indices:
+        return torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    return torch.cat(indices).to(device=device)
+
+

+def gather_mla_cache_tokens(
+    cache: torch.Tensor,
+    block_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    token_indices: torch.Tensor | None,
+    *,
+    is_nz: bool,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return [sum(prefix_lens), 1, head_dim], excluding every page tail.
+
+    Restore NZ token order before compacting. Truncating the concatenated
+    pages would retain padding between requests and shift their boundaries.
+    Pass None when all request lengths are page-aligned to skip compaction.
+    """
+    if block_ids.numel() == 0 or (
+        token_indices is not None and token_indices.numel() == 0
+    ):
+        return cache.new_empty((0, 1, cache.shape[-1]))
+    pages = gather_mla_cache_pages(cache, block_ids, is_nz=is_nz)
+    tokens = pages.flatten(0, 1)
+    if token_indices is None:
+        return tokens
+    # Match page gathering: FP8 copies use bytes until cache dequantization.
+    backing = (
+        tokens.view(torch.uint8) if tokens.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn else tokens
+    )
+    return torch.index_select(backing, 0, token_indices).view(cache.dtype)

+class TestMlaPrefixCacheDcp(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_fp8_prefix_dequantized_before_projection_or_dcp_gather(self):

+                (torch.arange(blocks * page * 32).remainder(97) - 48)

+                request_ids = ids[offset : offset + count]

+                expected_pe.append(rope[request_ids].flatten(0, 1)[:length])
+                offset += count
+            expected_k = torch.cat(expected_k)

+            for is_nz in (False, True):

+                        .reshape_as(backing)

+"""MLA prefix compaction across partially filled request pages.
+
+CPU: python -m pytest test/registered/unit/npu/attention/test_npu_mla_prefix_cache.py
+NPU: run the same command with SGLANG_TEST_NPU=1 in an Ascend environment.
+"""
+
+import os
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.attention.mla_cache import (
+    build_mla_prefix_token_indices,
+    gather_mla_cache_tokens,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+DEVICES = ["cpu"]
+if os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_NPU") == "1":
+    import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
+
+    DEVICES.append("npu")
+
+
+class TestNpuMlaPrefixCache(unittest.TestCase):
+    def check_gather(
+        self, lengths, page_size, head_dim, dtype, device, is_nz, *, compact=True
+    ):
+        counts = [(length + page_size - 1) // page_size for length in lengths]
+        total_pages = sum(counts)
+        # Repeat a shared block and visit physical pages out of order.
+        block_ids = [3, 1, 3, 0, 6, 2, 5, 4][:total_pages]
+        pages = torch.arange(8 * page_size * head_dim, dtype=torch.float32)
+        pages = pages.remainder(1009)
+        is_fp8 = dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        if is_fp8:
+            pages = pages.remainder(97) - 48
+        pages = pages.reshape(8, page_size, 1, head_dim).to(dtype)
+        reference_pages = pages.float() if is_fp8 else pages
+        expected_parts = []
+        block_start = 0
+        for length, count in zip(lengths, counts, strict=True):
+            request_pages = block_ids[block_start : block_start + count]
+            expected_parts.append(reference_pages[request_pages].flatten(0, 1)[:length])
+            block_start += count
+        expected = torch.cat(expected_parts)
+
+        backing_pages = pages.view(torch.uint8) if is_fp8 else pages
+        if is_nz:
+            tile_size = 32 if is_fp8 else 16
+            storage = (
+                backing_pages.view(8, page_size, head_dim // tile_size, tile_size)
+                .permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
+                .contiguous()
+                .view_as(backing_pages)
+            )
+        else:
+            # Also cover a noncontiguous ND view, as in sliced cache buffers.
+            backing = torch.empty(
+                8, page_size, 1, head_dim * 2, dtype=backing_pages.dtype
+            )
+            storage = backing[..., ::2]
+            storage.copy_(backing_pages)
+        if is_fp8:
+            storage = storage.view(dtype)
+
+        indices = (
+            build_mla_prefix_token_indices(
+                lengths, page_size, device=torch.device(device)
+            )
+            if compact
+            else None
+        )
+        with patch(
+            "sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.attention.mla_cache.torch.index_select",
+            wraps=torch.index_select,
+        ) as select:
+            actual = gather_mla_cache_tokens(
+                storage.to(device),
+                torch.tensor(block_ids, device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+                indices,
+                is_nz=is_nz,
+            )
+        expected_selects = 0 if sum(lengths) == 0 else 1 + int(compact)
+        self.assertEqual(select.call_count, expected_selects)
+        self.assertEqual(actual.shape, (sum(lengths), 1, head_dim))
+        self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, dtype)
+        if indices is not None:
+            self.assertEqual(indices.dtype, torch.int64)
+        actual_cpu = actual.cpu().float() if is_fp8 else actual.cpu()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_cpu, expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+    def test_fp8_aligned_and_partial_prefixes(self):
+        for device in DEVICES:
+            for is_nz in (False, True):
+                for lengths, page, head_dim in (
+                    ([5, 3, 0], 4, 32),
+                    ([4, 8, 0], 4, 64),
+                    ([128, 255, 129], 128, 512),
+                    ([0, 0], 4, 32),
+                ):
+                    with self.subTest(device=device, is_nz=is_nz, lengths=lengths):
+                        self.check_gather(
+                            lengths,
+                            page,
+                            head_dim,
+                            torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+                            device,
+                            is_nz,
+                            compact=any(length % page for length in lengths),
+                        )
+
+    def test_aligned_prefixes_skip_token_compaction(self):
+        for device in DEVICES:
+            for is_nz in (False, True):
+                for lengths, page, head_dim, dtype in (
+                    ([4, 8, 0], 4, 32, torch.float32),
+                    ([128, 0, 256], 128, 512, torch.bfloat16),
+                    ([0, 0], 4, 32, torch.float32),
+                ):
+                    with self.subTest(device=device, is_nz=is_nz, lengths=lengths):
+                        self.check_gather(
+                            lengths, page, head_dim, dtype, device, is_nz, compact=False
+                        )
+
+    def test_partial_middle_page_and_shared_blocks(self):
+        for device in DEVICES:
+            for is_nz in (False, True):
+                for lengths in ([3, 5, 1], [4, 3, 5], [5, 4, 3]):
+                    with self.subTest(device=device, is_nz=is_nz, lengths=lengths):
+                        self.check_gather(lengths, 4, 32, torch.float32, device, is_nz)
+
+    def test_zero_and_aligned_prefixes(self):
+        for device in DEVICES:
+            for is_nz in (False, True):
+                for lengths in ([0, 1, 3], [4, 0, 8], [0, 0]):
+                    with self.subTest(device=device, is_nz=is_nz, lengths=lengths):
+                        self.check_gather(lengths, 4, 32, torch.float32, device, is_nz)
+
+    def test_real_page_and_latent_rope_dimensions(self):
+        for device in DEVICES:
+            for is_nz in (False, True):
+                for head_dim in (64, 512):
+                    with self.subTest(device=device, is_nz=is_nz, head_dim=head_dim):
+                        self.check_gather(
+                            [128, 255, 129],
+                            128,
+                            head_dim,
+                            torch.bfloat16,
+                            device,
+                            is_nz,
+                        )
+
+    def test_indices_skip_each_request_tail(self):
+        indices = build_mla_prefix_token_indices(
+            [3, 5, 1], 4, device=torch.device("cpu")
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(indices.tolist(), [0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
